title: I'm working on a pixel art JRPG Roguelite, here is a combat trailer.
author: CinderleafDev
selftext:
I've been working for about a month on this project and finally now feel I'm settling into a rhythm where I'm happy enough with quality to focus on expanding content, rather than refining what I have. Obviously everything is still going to be polished to hell and back a few more times. 

As a result of that I had made a small combat demo of one of the currently finished bosses you can encounter in a special event (if you're unlucky!). 

I've had Claude prepare a trailer using some of the moves that heroes use in the battle.

Just to be clear, the game is long, long ways from being finished. This isn't a project I plan to wrap up in a month, two, three or even four most likely. A lot is being done and is already done in background and whole mode is already planned out.

comments.author: joeban1
comments.body: Looks awesome, how’d you make the art and vfx

replies.author: CinderleafDev
replies.body:
Basically, Claude sketches the poses from my description (or from a photo reference when it can’t figure the pose out on its own). The sketches are rough grey stand-ins placed next to the character’s main art. Before sketching, it writes a short plan for the move: where the hit lands, where the weight goes, what the free arm is doing. It also checks the plan against a list of rules built from every mistake I’ve caught so far. Then it sends things to Codex, which paints a few tries, and I pick the one I like. Claude converts that to pixels and matches it to the character’s main art (same palette, same size). Then a long list of checks runs: scripts for things like frames popping, feet floating or arms changing length, plus a second Claude agent that reviews it. Everything gets fixed, and it goes into the game once I approve the whole move on a preview page. I still have the power to adjust every frame by hand and have to do it sometimes (with a pixel editor Claude made for me).

VFX: a mix of code for the smaller impact attacks, switching to Codex for bigger effects and motions, done with Claude (again converted to pixel style and adjusted by hand). The code effects are drawn on the same pixel grid as the sprites, so everything matches.
